text:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion $𝐀$ and the other is labelled as Reason $𝐑$.

Assertion A: The spin only magnetic moment value for $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$ is $1.74\mathrm{BM}$, whereas for $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}$ is $5.92\mathrm{BM}$.

Reason $𝐑$ : In both complexes, $\mathrm{Fe}$ is present in +3 oxidation state.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In both complexes Fe is in the +3 state ($3d^{5}$), so R is true.

$\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ is a strong-field ligand: in $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ the five d electrons are arranged as $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$ ($d^{2}sp^{3}$), leaving 1 unpaired electron, so $μ=\sqrt{1(1+2)}=\sqrt{3}\approx 1.73\text{BM}$.


[IMG]

$\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is a weak-field ligand: in $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$ the configuration is $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$ with 5 unpaired electrons, so $μ=\sqrt{5(5+2)}=\sqrt{35}\approx 5.92\text{BM}$; hence A is true.

Since Fe has the same oxidation state in both complexes, the oxidation state cannot account for the different moments; the difference arises from the different field strengths of $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ and $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, so R is not the correct explanation of A.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: The standard electrode potential of $\mathrm{M}^{+}/\mathrm{M}$ in aqueous solution does not depend on
options: Ionisation of a gaseous metal atom
Ionisation of a solid metal atom
Hydration of a gaseous metal ion
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The electrode potential of $\mathrm{M}{}^{+}/\mathrm{M}$ reflects the overall enthalpy of $\mathrm{M}\quad (\mathrm{s})\longrightarrow \mathrm{M}{}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{e}{}^{-}$, which is made up of three steps:

$\mathrm{M}\quad (\mathrm{s})\longrightarrow \mathrm{M}(\mathrm{g})\Delta _{\text{sub}}H\text{(sublimation of the solid metal)}$

$\mathrm{M}\quad (\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow \mathrm{M}{}^{+}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\Delta _{i}H\text{(ionisation of the gaseous atom)}$

$\mathrm{M}{}^{+}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow \mathrm{M}{}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})\Delta _{\text{hyd}}H\text{(hydration of the gaseous ion)}$

Ionisation enthalpy always refers to an isolated gaseous atom; ionisation of an atom in the solid metal is not a step of this cycle, so $E^{\circ }$ does not depend on it.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

For a noble gas (positive value) and a halogen (negative value), the difference is the sum of the two magnitudes, so it is largest for the most positive noble gas (Ne) with the most negative halogen (Cl).

Ar and Cl: $96+349=445$; Ne and Cl: $116+349=465$; Ne and F: $116+328=444$; Ar and F: $96+328=424$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

Compound $\mathrm{P}$ is neutral, $\mathrm{Q}$ gives effervescence with $\mathrm{NaHCO}_{3}$ while $\mathrm{R}$ reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to give solid soluble in $\mathrm{NaOH}$. Compound $\mathrm{P}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
P ($\mathrm{C}{}_{14}\mathrm{H}{}_{13}\mathrm{ON}$) is neutral and is hydrolysed by hot HCl into an acid Q and an amine R, so P is an amide.

Q gives effervescence of $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$ with $\mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}$, so it is a carboxylic acid; it does not dissolve in the acid and remains as the residue. R stays in the filtrate as its hydrochloride and is set free by NaOH as an oily liquid.

The Hinsberg product of R dissolves in NaOH, so it still has an acidic N–H and R is a primary amine.

4-Methyl-N-phenylbenzamide fits: hydrolysis gives $p$-toluic acid (Q) and anilinium chloride, from which NaOH frees aniline (R).

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}\mathrm{CONHC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}+\mathrm{HCl}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}\mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}{}^{+}\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$


[IMG]

Amide (A) would give N-methylaniline, a secondary amine whose Hinsberg product is insoluble in NaOH.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: Strong reducing and oxidizing agents among the following, respectively, are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Strong reducing agents are those that readily donate electrons, and strong oxidizing agents are those that readily accept electrons.

$\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$: It can accept an electron to form $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$, so it is a strong oxidizing agent.

$\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$: It can donate an electron to form $\mathrm{Eu}^{3+}$, so it is a strong reducing agent.

So the correct answer is: $\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$.

Match List I with List II

Reagent used / Product formed

  

  
    A.

    I.

    B.
    Sulphur
    II.
    $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$
  
  
    C.
    Phosphorous
    III.
    $\mathrm{Fe}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]_{3}$
  
  
    D.
    Halogen
    IV.
    $(\mathrm{NH}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{MoO}_{4}$
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Nitrogen Detection (Lassaigne's Test)

Nitrogen in organic compounds is detected by converting it into sodium cyanide, which further reacts with iron(II) sulfate to form sodium hexacyanoferrate(II). By reacting this with iron(III) ions, Prussian blue is formed:

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Na}+\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{N}\to \mathrm{NaCN} \\  \\ 6\mathrm{NaCN}+\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}\to \mathrm{Na}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]+\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4} \\  \\ \mathrm{Na}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]+\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\to \mathrm{Fe}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]_{3}\text{(Prussian blue)} \end{array}$

Sulphur Detection

Sulphur can be detected using Sodium nitroprusside:

$\mathrm{Na}_{2}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{5}\mathrm{NO}]+\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{S}\to \mathrm{Na}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{5}\mathrm{NOS}]\text{[Purple]}$

Phosphorous Detection

Phosphorus detection involves reaction with ammonium molybdate to form a canary yellow compound:

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}+3\mathrm{HNO}_{3}\to \mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}+3\mathrm{NaNO}_{3} \\  \\ \mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}+12(\mathrm{NH}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{MoO}_{4}+21\mathrm{HNO}_{3}\to  \\  \\ (\mathrm{NH}_{4})_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}\cdot 12\mathrm{MoO}_{3}+21\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{NO}_{3}+12\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\text{(canary yellow)} \end{array}$

Halogen Detection

Halogens react with silver nitrate to form specific colored precipitates:

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}(\mathrm{aq})\to \mathrm{AgCl}+\mathrm{NaNO}_{3}\text{(White)} \\  \\ \mathrm{NaBr}+\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}(\mathrm{aq})\to \mathrm{AgBr}+\mathrm{NaNO}_{3}\text{(Pale yellow)} \\  \\ \mathrm{NaI}+\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}(\mathrm{aq})\to \mathrm{AgI}+\mathrm{NaNO}_{3}\text{(Yellow)} \end{array}$

Based on the above reactions, the correct matching is:

Option A

A-III (Nitrogen), B-I (Sulphur), C-IV (Phosphorous), D-II (Halogen).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text:
The wavelength of an electron of kinetic energy $4.50\times 10^{-29}$ J is $_________$ $\times 10^{-5}$ m. (Nearest integer)

Given : mass of electron is $9\times 10^{-31}$ kg, h $=6.6\times 10^{-34}$ J s
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} λ_{\mathrm{d}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{mv}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2\mathrm{mKE}}}=\dfrac{6.6\times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2\times 9\times 10^{-31}\times 4.5\times 10^{-29}}} \\  \\ =\dfrac{6.6\times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{9^{2}\times 10^{-60}}} \\  \\ =\dfrac{6.6\times 10^{-34}}{9\times 10^{-30}}=\dfrac{6.6}{9}\times 10^{-4} \\  \\ =7.3\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{m} \end{array}$

Therefore Ans $=7$

text:
The number of species from the following which have square pyramidal structure is $_________$

$\mathrm{PF}_{5},\mathrm{BrF}_{4}^{-},\mathrm{IF}_{5},\mathrm{BrF}_{5},\mathrm{XeOF}_{4},\mathrm{ICl}_{4}^{-}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A square pyramidal structure has five bonds and one lone pair, making a total of six electron pairs around the central atom. The geometry of such a molecule can be analyzed using the VSEPR theory.

$\mathrm{PF}_{5}$: 5 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs, so its geometry is trigonal bipyramidal, not square pyramidal.

$\mathrm{BrF}_{4}^{-}$: 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs, so its geometry is square planar, not square pyramidal.

$\mathrm{IF}_{5}$: 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair, so its geometry is square pyramidal.

$\mathrm{BrF}_{5}$: 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair, so its geometry is square pyramidal.

$\mathrm{XeOF}_{4}$: 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair, so its geometry is square pyramidal.

$\mathrm{ICl}_{4}^{-}$: 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs, so its geometry is square planar, not square pyramidal.

So the number of species from the given list that have a square pyramidal structure is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text:
Mass of Urea $(\mathrm{NH}_{2}\mathrm{CONH}_{2})$ required to be dissolved in $1000\mathrm{g}$ of water in order to reduce the vapour pressure of water by $25%$ is $_________  g. ($Nearest integer)

Given: Molar mass of N, C, O and H are $14,12,16$ and $1\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ respectively
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a non-volatile solute, Raoult's law gives $P_{s}=x_{\text{water}}P^{0}$.

A 25% lowering means $P_{s}=0.75P^{0}$, so $x_{\text{water}}=0.75$ and $x_{\text{urea}}=0.25$.

$\dfrac{n_{\text{urea}}}{n_{\text{water}}}=\dfrac{x_{\text{urea}}}{x_{\text{water}}}=\dfrac{0.25}{0.75}=\dfrac{1}{3}$

This is the exact relation $\dfrac{P^{0}-P_{s}}{P_{s}}=\dfrac{n_{\text{urea}}}{n_{\text{water}}}$; the dilute form with $P^{0}$ in the denominator does not hold for so large a lowering.

$n_{\text{water}}=\dfrac{1000}{18}=55.56\text{mol}$, so $n_{\text{urea}}=\dfrac{55.56}{3}=18.52\text{mol}$.

Molar mass of $\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CONH}{}_{2}$ $=2(14)+4(1)+12+16=60\text{g mol}^{-1}$.

$\text{Mass of urea}=18.52\times 60=1111\text{g}$

Hence, the answer is 1111.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text:
The value of $\log \mathrm{K}$ for the reaction $\mathrm{A}⇌\mathrm{B}$ at $298\mathrm{K}$ is $___________. ($Nearest integer)

Given: $\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ }=-54.07\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta \mathrm{S}^{\circ }=10\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

(Take $2.303\times 8.314\times 298=5705$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given:

$\begin{array}{ll} \Delta H^{0} & =-54.07\text{kJ/mol}=-54070\text{J/mol} \\  \\ \Delta S^{0} & =10\text{J/K}\cdot \text{mol} \\  \\ T & =298\text{K} \end{array}$

We find the change in Gibbs free energy $\Delta G^{0}$:

$\begin{array}{ll} \Delta G^{0} & =\Delta H^{0}-T\Delta S^{0} \\  \\ \qquad =-54070-(10\times 298) \\  \\ \qquad =-54070-2980 \\  \\ \qquad =-57050\text{J/mol} \end{array}$

Now, we'll use the given expression with the correct constant for $R$ as 8.314 J/(mol·K):

$\begin{array}{ll} \Delta G^{0} & =-2.303\times 8.314\times 298\times \log K \\  \\ \log K & =\dfrac{-57050}{2.303\times 8.314\times 298} \\  \\ \approx 10 \end{array}$

So, the answer is $\log K=10$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text:
Number of ambidentate ligands in a representative metal complex $[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{en})(\mathrm{SCN})_{4}]$ is $___________$.

[en = ethylenediamine]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ambidentate ligands are ligands that can bond to a metal atom through two different atoms. They can attach through one site or the other, but not both at the same time.

In the given complex $[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{en})(\mathrm{SCN})_{4}]$:

$\mathrm{en}$, or ethylenediamine, is a bidentate ligand, meaning it can form two bonds with the metal ion, but it is not ambidentate because it always binds through the same two nitrogen atoms.

$\mathrm{SCN}^{-}$, on the other hand, is an example of an ambidentate ligand. It can bind to the metal either through the sulfur atom ($\mathrm{S}$) or the nitrogen atom ($\mathrm{N}$).

Since there are four $\mathrm{SCN}^{-}$ ligands in the given complex, the number of ambidentate ligands is 4.

text: If 5 moles of $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ is mixed with 2 moles of $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}$, the maximum number of moles of $\mathrm{Ba}_{3}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}$ formed is $___________ ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given the balanced chemical equation:

$3\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}+2\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}\to \mathrm{Ba}_{3}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}+6\mathrm{NaCl}$

We can see that 3 moles of $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ react with 2 moles of $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}$ to produce 1 mole of $\mathrm{Ba}_{3}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}$.

Given that you have 5 moles of $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ and 2 moles of $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}$, let's calculate the maximum number of moles of $\mathrm{Ba}_{3}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}$ that can be formed:

From $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$, using the molar ratio from the balanced equation: 

$5\text{moles}\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}\times \frac{1\text{mole}\mathrm{Ba}_{3}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}}{3\text{moles}\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}}=\frac{5}{3}\text{moles}\mathrm{Ba}_{3}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}$

From $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}$, using the molar ratio from the balanced equation:

$2\text{moles}\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}\times \frac{1\text{mole}\mathrm{Ba}_{3}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}}{2\text{moles}\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}}=1\text{mole}\mathrm{Ba}_{3}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}$

The limiting reactant is $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}$ because it produces 1 mole of $\mathrm{Ba}_{3}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}$, which is less than the $\frac{5}{3}$ moles produced by $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$.

Therefore, the maximum number of moles of $\mathrm{Ba}_{3}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}$ formed is 1 mole. Rounding to the nearest integer, the answer is 1.

text: In ammonium - phosphomolybdate, the oxidation state of Mo is $+ ___________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: In ammonium phosphomolybdate, the compound typically found in the reagent used for the quantitative determination of phosphorus, the molybdenum (Mo) atom is in the +6 oxidation state.
